title: Advanced Link Attributes
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of advanced link attributes in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Advanced Link Attributes” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with the target attribute, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Text, links, lists, images, and media are the building blocks of readable, navigable web content; the markup should communicate meaning even before CSS is added.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Text, links, lists, images, and media are the building blocks of readable, navigable web content; the markup should communicate meaning even before CSS is added.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The target attribute: the browsing context to use; opening new tabs should be a deliberate choice.

items.title: The target attribute
items.text: The target attribute: the browsing context to use; opening new tabs should be a deliberate choice.

items.title: The rel attribute
items.text: The rel attribute: the relationship between the current document and the destination, often used to add security or meaning.

items.title: The download attribute
items.text: The download attribute is one of the decisions covered by Advanced Link Attributes. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: The hreflang attribute
items.text: The hreflang attribute is one of the decisions covered by Advanced Link Attributes. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: The type attribute
items.text: The type attribute: a value that can select an input mode or describe a linked resource; valid values depend on the element.

items.title: The referrerpolicy attribute
items.text: The referrerpolicy attribute: controls referrer information sent with requests or navigation.

items.title: Safe new-tab links and opener considerations
items.text: Resolve the URL relative to the current document or base URL. Prefer meaningful link text, test internal paths from each page location, and verify external destinations.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates advanced link attributes. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Advanced Link Attributes.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for advanced link attributes.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.
content.expected_output: The first two links open local pages when those files exist; the fragment link jumps to the Contact section.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Advanced Link Attributes is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.
Resolve the URL relative to the current document or base URL. Prefer meaningful link text, test internal paths from each page location, and verify external destinations.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
